title: Kepler's third law across exoplanets
question: Per planet in the NASA Exoplanet Archive composite table: is log₁₀ P² a straight line of slope 1 in log₁₀(a³/M★), and how far does each planet sit from it?

issues.text: For many transiting planets the archive computed a from P and M★ with Kepler's law, so those rows can't test it.
issues.fix: Report the share that agrees to <1% (log_ratio) and repeat the fit on the rest, and per discovery method.

issues.text: Imaging and microlensing planets, whose a is measured without the law, are few (about 40).
issues.fix: Read their spread as an upper bound and widen with the per-reference ps table.

alternatives.question: Is the slope of log P² on log(a³/M★) 1 for planets whose a disagrees with Kepler's law by more than 1%?
alternatives.why: Drops the rows computed with the law.

alternatives.question: Do the stellar masses from the orbit (m_kepler) of multi-planet systems agree with the archive's M★ within 10%?
alternatives.why: Drills into systems, where several orbits weigh one star.

alternatives.question: Does the stellar density from transits, (a/R★)³/P², match M★/R★³?
alternatives.why: Expands to a law-free measurement of a/R★ from the light curve.

hypotheses.statement: log₁₀ P² rises with log₁₀(a³/M★) with slope 1.
hypotheses.null: The slope differs from 1 (the period does not follow a³/M★).

predictor.concept: Semi-major axis cubed over star mass

hypotheses.statement: Without dividing by M★, log P against log a has slope 1.5 only if the stars' masses don't change with a.

concepts.label: Planet
concepts.description: A confirmed exoplanet, one row of pscomppars.

concepts.label: Orbital period
concepts.description: P, days in the archive, years here.

concepts.label: Stellar mass
concepts.description: M★ in solar masses, from the star's spectrum and stellar models.

concepts.label: Dynamical mass
concepts.description: a³/P²: the star's mass as the orbit weighs it.
concepts.why: Compares the law with the catalogue.

concepts.label: Discovery method
concepts.why: Decides whether a was measured or computed.

data.request: The ps table's rows per planet and reference (default_flag 0 and 1), with pl_orbsmax, st_mass and their reference links
data.source: NASA Exoplanet Archive TAP, table ps
data.why: To separate the papers whose a is computed from the law.

method.summary: A straight line of log P² on log(a³/M★) with a weak prior; the posterior of the slope against 1.

steps.title: Planets from pscomppars
steps.detail: pl_orbper, pl_orbsmax, st_mass for every planet that has all three.

steps.title: Measured or computed a
steps.detail: |log_ratio| < 0.0043 marks rows whose a was likely computed from P and M★.

steps.title: Fit both lines
steps.detail: log_p on log_a (expect 1.5 only for equal stars) and log_p2 on log_a3_m (expect 1).

steps.title: Slope against 1
steps.detail: On all planets and on those with |log_ratio| ≥ 0.0043.

caveats: About half the semi-major axes were computed with the law being tested.
Composite rows mix references: P, a and M★ may come from different papers.
The planet's mass is neglected; for brown-dwarf companions it is a few percent of M★.
Projected separations (imaging) are lower bounds on a.
